name: telar-desktop
//productName: NAMES THE USER-DATA DIRECTORY, not just the window. Electron's app.getName() prefers this over `name`, and app.getPath('userData') is composed from it — so without it this app's state lives in ~/Library/Application Support/telar-desktop, a directory named after the shell package rather than the product. That directory is now TELAR_HOME for a packaged build (main.js), which makes the name a thing people will read.
description: Telar desktop shell with a shared Electron-owned browser host.
author: Facundo Barbera <facundo.barbera@gmail.com>

scripts.//test:desktop:unit: --timeout IS THE CEILING FOR THIS WORKSPACE, because this is the one workspace with no bunfig.toml. `[test] timeout` is still not a bunfig key — bun ignores unknown keys silently, and #414 shipped exactly that for apps/engine — but `preload` is, which is how apps/engine and apps/web now reach the shared ceiling in scripts/test-ceiling.mjs (#740) and how a bare `bun test apps/desktop/one.test.js` typed from the repo root reaches it too. Only a run whose cwd is this directory depends on the flag below; where the preload does load it reads an explicit `--timeout` back off the operating system and stands aside for it, so the flag means the same thing in both places. `test-ceiling-is-registered` in scripts/source-invariants.mjs keeps its number equal to that file's. 20 s because these are the Electron-free unit tests but several still spawn real processes — packaging.test.js runs package-desktop.sh and extracts an asar through bunx — and the credential-lifecycle tests poll a real ~750 ms probe. On the shared CI Mac mini that crosses 5 s for a reason that has nothing to do with the code (#458).
scripts.//test:desktop:unit:glob: A GLOB, NOT A LIST OF NAMES. This was 36 filenames typed out by hand, and `push-relay.test.js` — eight tests about writing a relay token to the Keychain without putting it in argv where `ps` shows it — was never added to them, so it had never once run in CI (#760 §7). A hand-list fails in both directions: a new file is dark until somebody remembers it, and a file DELETED while still named here fails the whole suite for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. `./*.test.js` has neither failure mode. THE ELECTRON TESTS ARE EXCLUDED BY THEIR OWN NAME, not by an exclusion list: they are `*.electron-test.js`, and `*.test.js` cannot match that — the character before `test.js` is a hyphen, not a dot. They run in the `electron` CI job instead. ONE STAR, NOT TWO: `**` would descend into node_modules; apps/desktop is flat and a test in a new subdirectory would need this line changed, which is the trade accepted here.

extendInfo.//NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: The string macOS shows in the Automation consent dialog when Telar first drives Codex's Computer Use client. Without it the prompt cannot appear and every computer-use call fails silently with -1743.
extendInfo.NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: Telar uses Computer Use to control Mac apps on your behalf — taking screenshots and performing clicks and keystrokes — through Codex's Computer Use client.
extendInfo.//NSCameraUsageDescription: The string macOS shows the FIRST time a page in Telar's browser asks for the camera (systemPreferences.askForMediaAccess). Without it the request is refused before any dialog can appear, and the page reports NotAllowedError as though a person had said no — which is exactly what #422 was: camera and microphone were never offered, not broken.
extendInfo.NSCameraUsageDescription: Telar's built-in browser needs the camera for sites you allow it on — video calls and anything that asks. Telar asks you per site first, and never turns the camera on by itself.
extendInfo.//NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: The microphone half of the same gate. Both strings must be in the packaged Info.plist; a signed build without them denies silently rather than prompting.
extendInfo.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Telar's built-in browser needs the microphone for sites you allow it on — calls, dictation and anything that asks. Telar asks you per site first, and never listens by itself.
